review_focus: Every route by which URI could contact or show content from a host with non-English letters: user URLs, search hits (all providers), redirects (absolute, relative, scheme-relative, percent-encoded or IDNA-mapped Location values), feeds, robots.txt, social instances, proxy egress. Any bypass of HOST_NON_ENGLISH (e.g. Unicode that IDNA maps to ASCII, dots like U+3002, uppercase XN--, trailing dot, ports) is blocking.
Regressions for ASCII hosts: no genuine ASCII host, IP literal or existing refusal code may change behaviour (HOST_NUMERIC_AMBIGUOUS for full-width digits must stay).

The user-facing note (D18 brief, plain words; D21 must say why): shown once whenever any site was blocked, A2UI-valid, never contains the address or anything clickable; blocked_non_english counts are right (no double counting of one site, no count for non-IDN refusals).

O2 Hebrew points: SHIN DOT / SIN DOT allowed only on a Hebrew letter; any way to use them to disguise a link (alone, on another script, between name and ending, repeated) must still be caught. Do not reopen the D30/D31-closed link class beyond this change.
